items.claim: Delivery Hero announces divestment of its Taiwan food delivery operations to Grab for cash.
items.quote: to Grab for USD 600 million in cash
items.speaker: L. Östberg (CEO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CEO frames the Taiwan sale to Grab as Delivery Hero's fifth asset monetization to date.
items.quote: This is our fifth asset monetization to date
items.speaker: L. Östberg (CEO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CFO gives expected closing timeline for the Grab-Taiwan transaction.
items.quote: the transaction will close in the second half of 2026
items.speaker: Marie-Anne Popp (CFO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: Delivery Hero commits to a transitional services period supporting the Taiwan business after close.
items.quote: a migration period of up to 12 months following the close
items.speaker: L. Östberg (CEO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CFO states the EBITDA and cash flow impact of losing the Taiwan business will be marginal for Delivery Hero during the TSA period.
items.quote: the impact on the EBITDA and cash flow would be marginal
items.speaker: Marie-Anne Popp (CFO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CEO contrasts Uber's prior in-market Taiwan bid with Grab's market-entry position when discussing deal multiple.
items.quote: Uber was and still is operating in the market
items.speaker: L. Östberg (CEO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CEO characterizes the agreed deal terms as favorable for Grab with further upside.
items.quote: a good deal that is a good boost for Grab
items.speaker: L. Östberg (CEO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CEO asserts the Taiwan business (being sold to Grab) holds a strong competitive position in its market.
items.quote: we have a very strong position in the Taiwan market
items.speaker: L. Östberg (CEO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CEO describes geographically uneven share split between the Taiwan business and Uber.
items.quote: There will be some areas where they will be slightly larger
items.speaker: L. Östberg (CEO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CFO indicates Delivery Hero's Singapore tech hub operations will need resizing over time following the Taiwan divestment.
items.quote: there will definitely be a process of adjusting
items.speaker: Marie-Anne Popp (CFO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CFO discloses FY2025 GMV scale of the Taiwan business being acquired by Grab.
items.quote: generated a GMV of EUR 1.5 billion
items.speaker: Marie-Anne Popp (CFO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CFO states the Taiwan sale proceeds reduce Delivery Hero's net leverage ratio.
items.quote: reducing our net leverage from approximately 2.7x to 2.2x
items.speaker: Marie-Anne Popp (CFO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CEO signals the Taiwan sale is only the first of several ongoing Delivery Hero portfolio reviews, implying more divestment candidates could later reach the market.
items.quote: it is just one of several ongoing reviews
items.speaker: L. Östberg (CEO, Delivery Hero)

items.claim: CFO reiterates that raised term loan and sale proceeds are earmarked toward existing debt repayment.
items.quote: to focus on repaying existing debt
items.speaker: Marie-Anne Popp (CFO, Delivery Hero)

qa_flags.question: Why issue a $1.4B term loan, roughly $600M more than the stated convert buyback need, and why sit on such a large cash balance?
qa_flags.response_pattern: CFO repeats generic prior messaging ('strengthen capital structure', 'repay existing debt', 'remain flexible for future opportunities') without addressing the specific ~$600M gap the analyst asked about.

qa_flags.question: Does the Taiwan sale unlock a larger evolution/reduction in central and tech (Singapore hub) costs over time?
qa_flags.response_pattern: CFO does not confirm, deny, or quantify any central-cost reduction; reiterates that hub sizing is 'an ongoing process' and support continues through the TSA period.
